q: According to KOC.SA.002, how often must an in-service scaffold be re-inspected by an authorized Scaffolding Inspector, whether or not it has been used?
options: Only after alterations or bad weather
source: Cl. 4.1.3 / 5.1.6: inspection before first use, after alteration, after adverse weather and every 7 days thereafter.

q: Above what wind speed does KOC.SA.002 prohibit work on or from scaffolds?
source: Cl. 5.1.3 c): work on scaffolds is prohibited during storms or high winds (wind speed more than 65 km/h).

q: An elevated scaffold work area requires at least two means of exit when the horizontal travel distance to the nearest exit ladder exceeds:
source: Cl. 5.1.3 f): where horizontal travel distance to the nearest exit exceeds 15 m (50 ft), at least two means of exit are required.

q: A worker is setting up a portable ladder against a structure. Which set-up ratio meets the KOC.SA.002 requirement of approximately 76 degrees?
options: 1 m out for every 2 m up
1 m out for every 3 m up
1 m out for every 4 m up
1 m out for every 6 m up
source: Cl. 5.2.2 h): ladders shall be set at an angle of 76 degrees (1 m out for 4 m up).

q: Where no adequate handhold is provided at the landing, a portable ladder must extend above the landing place by at least:
source: Cl. 5.2.2 i): the ladder must rise at least 1.05 m (3.5 ft) above the landing place.

q: Without a supporting risk assessment, what is the minimum distance a scaffold may be erected from an existing excavation?
source: Cl. 5.1.3 aa): no scaffold shall be erected less than 3 m from an existing excavation; a shorter distance only based on a risk assessment.

q: What minimum experience does KOC.SA.002 require for a Scaffolding Supervisor, in addition to certified erection and dismantling training?
options: 3 years in scaffolding, with no supervisory requirement
5 years in scaffolding, including at least 1 year as a supervisor
5 years in scaffolding, including at least 3 years as a supervisor
10 years in scaffolding, including at least 2 years as a supervisor
source: Cl. 5.1.2 b): minimum 5 years' experience in scaffolding jobs, of which at least one year in a supervisory role.

q: What is the maximum permitted height of a portable stepladder under KOC.SA.002?
source: Cl. 5.2.3 f): portable stepladders shall not exceed 20 ft (6.1 m) in height.

q: What is the maximum validity of a Hot, Cold or Radiography Work Permit from its date of issue, subject to renewal by the Permit Issuer?
source: Cl. 5.4: Hot / Cold / Radiography permits are valid for a maximum of seven consecutive days from the date of issue, subject to renewal.

q: A Work Permit endorsement or renewal remains valid for a maximum of:
source: Cl. 5.8 e): each endorsement / renewal is valid for a maximum of one shift (12 hours) or as recorded by the Permit Issuer.

q: A worksite was gas tested and certified gas free at 07:00, but the job could not start until 09:30. What must happen before work starts?
options: Work may start because the certificate is valid for the shift
Work may start if the Worksite Supervisor signs the permit
A new gas test must be carried out
Work may start if a fire watch is posted
source: Cl. 5.15 b): if work has not started within 2 hours of a gas test, the gas free certification becomes invalid and a new test is required.

q: What is the maximum flammable gas reading permitted for authorizing Hot Work under the KOC Permit to Work Procedure?
source: Cl. 5.13.2 / 5.15 g): the maximum LEL permissible for authorized Hot Work is 0% LEL.

q: During cold work on a flowline, 0% LEL cannot be achieved despite depressurizing, venting and purging. Under what condition may the work proceed?
options: Below 10% LEL, continuously monitored, with an approved Method Statement
Below 20% LEL, with all workers wearing breathing apparatus sets
Below 25% LEL, with a fire watch and extinguishers posted at site
Any LEL reading, with verbal approval from the Permit Issuer
source: Cl. 5.13.1 c): work may be carried out ensuring LEL does not exceed 10% under continuous monitoring; a reviewed and approved Method Statement is mandatory.

q: What is the maximum period a Work Permit can remain suspended before it must be cancelled and signed off?
options: 24 hours, after which it is cancelled
3 days, after which it is cancelled
5 days, or permit expiry if sooner
source: Cl. 5.11: a Work Permit can be suspended for a maximum of 5 days or until expiry of its validity, whichever is sooner.

q: What is the minimum fire extinguisher provision for each Hot Work location under KOC.SA.004?
source: Cl. 5.16 a): a minimum of two fire extinguishers (9 kg Monnex or 12 kg DCP) within 7.5 m of each hot work location.

q: Unless otherwise stated in the permit, how long is an Excavation Notification valid from the date the Asset Owner signs it?
source: Cl. 5.13.6 e): the Excavation Notification is valid for 90 days from the date of issuance.

q: What is the minimum passing score for the PTW qualifying written test for Permit Issuers, Permit Applicants and Worksite Supervisors?
source: Cl. 5.7 b): the passing score for the PTW qualifying test shall be a minimum of 70%.

q: Under KOC.SA.004, mechanical excavation is NOT allowed within what radius of any underground facility?
source: Cl. 5.13.6 a): mechanical excavation is not allowed inside the plant or facility or within 5 m radius of any underground facilities.

q: During a routine check, an SCBA breathing air cylinder gauge shows it has dropped below full charge. At what point does KOC.SA.005 require it to be sent for recharging?
options: When pressure falls to 90% of the specified pressure
When pressure falls to 75% of the specified pressure
When pressure falls to 50% of the specified pressure
source: Cl. 4.2 / 5.4.3: cylinder pressure must not be less than 90% of full capacity; refill when pressure drops to 90% of specified pressure.

q: When checking an SCBA, the cylinder valve is closed slowly to test the low-pressure warning alarm. At approximately what level of cylinder capacity should the alarm sound?
source: Cl. 5.4.5 C: verify activation of the low pressure alarm (to sound at approximately 25% of cylinder capacity).

q: What is the maximum validity of an RPE 'Authorized User Card' issued by the Controlling Team?
source: Cl. 5.4.4: validity of the Authorized User Card shall not exceed 12 months and must be within the medical examination validity.

q: What periodic hydrostatic test intervals does KOC.SA.005 specify for SCBA breathing air cylinders?
options: Steel every 3 years; composite every 5 years
Steel every 5 years; composite every 3 years
Steel and composite both every 5 years
Steel and composite both every 10 years
source: Cl. 5.4.5 C: verify SCBA cylinder is current on hydrostatic test (5 years for steel, 3 years for composite cylinders).

q: A worker passes a quantitative fit test with a full-face respirator. Which requirement then applies on the job?
options: Any model from the same manufacturer may be used
Any size of the same model may be used
The exact same make, model, style and size must be used
Any tight-fitting respirator with the same APF may be used
source: Cl. 5.7: after passing a fit test, the user must use the exact same make, model, style and size of respirator; fit testing is at least annual.

q: What minimum specification does KOC.SA.005 set for SCBA used by emergency services (Fire Group)?
options: Negative pressure type, minimum 30 minutes duration
Positive pressure type, minimum 30 minutes duration
Positive pressure type, minimum 45 minutes duration
Positive pressure type, minimum 60 minutes duration
source: Cl. 5.2.1 Note 1: SCBA for emergency services shall be positive pressure type with minimum 45 minutes duration, conforming to NFPA 1981.

q: An air-purifying respirator filter has been removed from its sealed packaging but rarely used. When must it be replaced, regardless of use?
source: Cl. 5.4.5 B: a filter once opened from the seal must be replaced after 6 months regardless of its use.

q: How often, at a minimum, must the output air quality of a breathing air compressor be checked?
options: Every month, and after each filter change
Every 3 months, and after each filter change
Every 6 months, and after each filter change
Every 12 months, and after each filter change
source: Cl. 5.9: periodic checks of compressor output air quality at least once every 3 months and after each filter change.

q: Which set of gas test results permits confined space entry WITHOUT respiratory protection under KOC.SA.007 Table 1?
source: Table 1: entry without respiratory protection when O2 is 19.5–23.5%, flammables < 10% LEL and H2S < 10 ppm.

q: Gas testing of a vessel shows 15% oxygen. According to KOC.SA.007 Table 1, what is the correct action?
options: Entry permitted with an air-purifying respirator
Entry permitted with forced ventilation only
Entry permitted with SCBA and continuous monitoring
No entry, except in an emergency or for rescue
source: Table 1: oxygen content less than 16% (or H2S > 100 ppm, or flammables 50% LEL or above) = NO ENTRY except emergency or rescue.

q: The initial confined space gas test was done at 08:00 but entry is delayed until 09:15. What does KOC.SA.007 require?
options: Entry may proceed because the test is valid for the shift
A follow-up gas test by the Worksite Supervisor before entry
A new Confined Space Entry Certificate must be raised
Entry may proceed if entrants wear personal H2S monitors
source: Cl. 5.3: entry is to take place within one hour of the initial gas test; otherwise a follow-up gas test by the Worksite Supervisor is required before entry.

q: Where periodic (rather than continuous) gas monitoring is used during a confined space entry, the interval between tests shall not exceed:
source: Cl. 5.13: the periodic monitoring of gas shall not exceed a two-hour period.

q: How frequently does KOC.SA.007 require personnel working inside a vessel or tank to be given a rest period, unless conditions require more frequent breaks?
source: Cl. 5.11: personnel working inside the vessel / tank will be given a rest period at each 30 minute interval, or more frequently.

q: Inside a KOC hydrocarbon facility, an excavation is classified as a confined space when its depth exceeds:
source: Cl. 2.0 c): excavation with depth more than 1.2 m inside hydrocarbon facilities is a confined space.

q: An entrant collapses inside a vessel. What is the correct immediate action for the standby person who is not trained in search and rescue?
options: Enter at once wearing an escape set and pull the entrant out
Summon aid via the Control Room and stay outside until relief arrives
Send another entrant inside to assist the casualty to the manway
Lower a spare SCBA set to the casualty and wait at the manway
source: Cl. 4.4 Note / 5.11: the standby person must not enter until relief arrives; he must summon aid immediately via the Control Room.

q: Which of the following must NEVER be used to ventilate a confined space?
source: Cl. 5.5: compressed oxygen or instrument air shall never be used to ventilate a confined space.

q: A vessel has been certified gas free but flammable residues may remain. If extra-low-voltage portable lighting is used, what is its maximum voltage under KOC.SA.007?
source: Cl. 5.6: such spaces may be illuminated by extra low voltage (25 V AC) portable lighting approved for Zone 1; transformers never taken inside.

q: On a bench-mounted grinder, what is the maximum gap permitted between the work rest and the abrasive wheel?
source: Cl. 5.1.2.1: work rest adjusted as close to the wheel as possible at a maximum distance of 1/4 inch.

q: The 'ring test' described in KOC.SA.012 for checking an abrasive wheel for cracks is applicable to which type of wheel?
options: Small wheels of 100 mm diameter or less
source: Cl. 5.1.2.3 / 5.1.2.5: the ring test is used only for vitrified bonded wheels; it is not practicable for small, mounted, segment or plate-mounted wheels.

q: After a new abrasive wheel is mounted, how long should it be allowed to run free, with users standing clear, before use?
source: Cl. 5.1.2.3: new wheels should be allowed to run free for about 60 seconds; users should stand clear.

q: A technician is selecting a cutting disc for a portable grinder. Which speed rating requirement must the disc meet?
options: Rated at or above the RPM of the grinder
Rated at 75% of the grinder RPM
Rated below the grinder RPM to reduce vibration
Any rating, provided a speed governor is fitted
source: Cl. 5.1.2.1: ensure speed of the wheel is compatible with the machine, i.e. use a wheel or disc rated at or above the RPM of the grinder.

q: Under KOC.SA.012, a mobile air compressor may be deployed in a Zone 2 hazardous area only:
options: Under a Cold Work Permit with continuous gas monitoring
Under a Hot Work Permit, if suitable for the area classification
Under a Vehicle Entry Permit, if a spark arrestor is fitted
It is never permitted in a Zone 2 area
source: Cl. 5.2.2: mobile compressors are not permitted in Zone 0 & 1; in Zone 2 they must be covered by an authorized Hot Work Permit, subject to suitability.

q: Which method of connecting a pneumatic tool to its high-pressure air hose is acceptable under KOC.SA.012?
options: Screw-adjusted 'Jubilee' clip, tightened with a screwdriver
Crowfoot coupling with retaining pin/clip and whip check
Wire-twisted joint secured with heavy-duty insulation tape
Push-fit coupling, with the hose tied to the tool handle
source: Cl. 5.2.1 / 5.2.3: purpose-made connections (e.g. crowfoot) with retaining pin/clip and whip; 'Jubilee' type connections are not permitted.

q: At or above what noise level from air compressors and pneumatic tools must warning signs be displayed and hearing protection worn?
source: Cl. 5.2.1: if noise levels are at or above 85 dB, signs must be displayed and hearing protection worn.

q: Abrasive wheels in a store have been in stock for more than two years. What does KOC.SA.012 recommend before they are issued?
options: Issue them only for light grinding work
Consult the manufacturer or supplier first
Ring test them all, including resin wheels
Discard them without any further assessment
source: Cl. 5.1.2.7: in case of doubt, or if wheels have been in stock for more than two years, the manufacturer/supplier should be consulted.

q: What is the maximum age of a contractor's mobile equipment or heavy vehicle permitted for work in KOC business under KOC.SA.013?
source: Cl. 5.2: contractor mobile equipment / heavy vehicles shall not be older than 20 years, subject to suitability and 3rd party certification.

q: How often must a contractor's mobile crane (load handling equipment) be inspected and certified by a KOC-approved inspection contractor?
options: Every 12 months or contract duration, whichever is earlier
source: Cl. 5.4 I a): general mobile equipment once a year (or contract duration if earlier); load or material handling equipment once every 6 months per KOC.SA.029.

q: A contractor's forklift is involved in a minor incident and then repaired. What does KOC.SA.013 require before it is used again?
options: The operator completes a pre-use checklist
A new Clearance Certificate based on a new inspection report
The existing Clearance Certificate is endorsed by the Area HSE Team
No action is needed for a minor incident
source: Cl. 4.6: after any incident or major repair / modification, a new Clearance Certificate is issued based on a new inspection report from a KOC-approved inspection contractor.

q: Under KOC.SA.013, gasoline-operated equipment such as a jumping compactor is restricted on site unless it is fitted with:
options: A reverse alarm and a reverse camera
Vibration-resistant fuel caps and spark arrestors
A dead-man switch and emergency stop button
source: Cl. 4.6: gasoline-operated equipment is restricted unless fitted with vibration-resistant fuel caps and spark arrestors.

q: In which areas does KOC.SA.013 require mobile equipment to hold a valid Clearance Certificate?
options: Only in Zone 0 and Zone 1 hazardous areas
Only in hazardous areas inside plant fences
In both hazardous and non-hazardous areas
Only for equipment with a State registration plate
source: Cl. 5.1: all mobile equipment shall require a Clearance Certificate for both hazardous and non-hazardous areas including Ahmadi area.

q: A contractor wants to move a generator from Contract A to Contract B, both under the same contractor, using Contract A's Clearance Certificate and Gate Pass. Under KOC.SA.013 this is:
options: Acceptable, since the contractor is the same
Acceptable, if the certificate is still valid
Not acceptable; it must be issued under Contract B
source: Cl. 4.6: contractor cannot use mobile equipment with another contract's Clearance Certificate and Gate Pass, even if the contractor is the same (drilling teams excepted).

q: During maintenance on a dump truck with a raised bed, which control does KOC.SA.013 require to protect personnel?
options: Lowering the bed onto stacked timber blocks
Fitting a mechanical locking device to the raised bed
Keeping the engine running so hydraulics hold the bed
Posting a banksman to watch the bed during work
source: Cl. 5.1.1 (2): no personnel under a raised bed; use appropriate mechanical locking devices during maintenance to prevent sudden bed movement.

q: Which precaution must be met before a heavy vehicle without an inbuilt spark arrestor is deployed at a KOC worksite?
options: Its exhaust tail pipe must be fitted with a spark arrestor
It must be parked at least 30 m from process equipment
Its engine must be switched off every 30 minutes
Its fuel tank must be at least half full
source: Cl. 5.1.1: the exhaust tail pipe is fitted with a spark arrestor in case it is not inbuilt.

q: In-service flange bolting replacement (hot bolting) is NOT permitted on flanges having fewer than how many bolts?
source: Cl. 5.3: in-service bolt replacement / rework is not permitted on flanges with less than six bolts.

q: Above what line pressure does KOC.SA.015 prohibit in-service flange bolting replacement?
source: Cl. 5.3: not permitted on high-pressure lines > 13.6 bar (200 psi) including air, nitrogen and hydrocarbons.

q: A gas line contains 800 ppm of H2S. Under KOC.SA.015, can in-service hot bolting be carried out on it?
options: Yes, if all workers wear SCBA
Yes, if line pressure is first reduced
No, it is in highly sour service
No, any line above 10 ppm is excluded
source: Cl. 2.0 / 5.3: highly sour service is > 500 ppm H2S; hot bolting is not permitted on systems in highly sour service.

q: During in-service bolt replacement on a live flange, how many bolts may be slackened at any one time?
options: Up to one quarter of the bolts
source: Cl. 5.3 d): slacken one bolt only; under no circumstances must two bolts be slackened at any one time.

q: When fitting new bolts during in-service bolt replacement (without tensioning equipment), how far may the bolt protrude beyond the nut?
options: No more than two full threads
No more than five full threads
source: Cl. 5.3 h): new bolts should protrude no more than two full threads beyond the nut.

q: While breaking a flange, the crew finds the bolts are badly corroded and will not turn. What is the only acceptable removal method under KOC.SA.015?
options: Gas cutting with an oxy-acetylene torch
Striking the nuts with an iron hammer
source: Cl. 5.4: if bolts are corroded, the only acceptable method is a pneumatic hacksaw; gas cutting (open flame) shall not be used.

q: What is the correct body position and first bolt to loosen when breaking a flange that may still contain pressure?
options: Stand downwind and loosen the bolts nearest to you
Stand upwind and loosen the bolts farthest away from you
Stand directly in front and loosen bolts clockwise
Stand upwind and loosen all bolts evenly at the same time
source: Cl. 5.2 o) / 5.5 a): maintain a safe upwind position and loosen bolts farthest away first so any release sprays away from the worker.

q: Which type of hammer may be used when breaking flanges on lines in hydrocarbon service?
options: Any hammer, if a fire watch is present
source: Cl. 5.4: do not use an iron hammer in hydrocarbon service because impact will generate sparks; only brass hammers shall be used.

q: A leak clamp has been installed on a process line. Within what period does KOC.SA.017 require the original integrity of the line to be restored?
source: Cl. 5.2: all clamps are temporary; appropriate actions shall be taken to restore original integrity within three months.

q: If permanent repair cannot be done within the initial period, a Clamp Joint Evaluation Meeting may authorize the clamp for a further maximum of:
source: Cl. 5.2 / 5.3: the Asset Owner may request extension through the Clamp Joint Evaluation Meeting for a maximum of six months after the initial three months.

q: How far in advance must the Asset Owner submit a Clamp Extension Request, with valid justification, before the agreed clamp period expires?
source: Cl. 5.4: request shall be submitted at least ten working days prior to exceeding the agreed period; authorization from Group Manager (Ops/GO).

q: Inspection finds that the leak on a pipeline is caused by a crack. What does KOC.SA.017 require?
options: Fit a bolt-on mechanical clamp rated for the MAOP
Fit a sealing band clamp centred on the crack
Do not clamp; replace the cracked spool with new pipe
Fit a split sleeve clamp and de-rate the line
source: Cl. 5.2: if a crack appears on any area of the piping, clamping shall not be used; the cracked portion shall be replaced with a new pipe spool.

q: What pressure capability must a bolt-on mechanical leak clamp have under KOC.SA.017?
options: At least 50% of the line's operating pressure
At least equal to the normal operating pressure only
Capable of containing the MAOP of the carrier pipe
Equal to the hydrotest pressure of the clamp only
source: Cl. 4.3 / 5.2: clamp design pressure not less than that of the piping; the clamp must be capable of containing the MAOP of the carrier pipe.

q: When sealing band clamps are used on isolated external corrosion pits, what is the minimum spacing between two such clamps?
options: No two clamps within one pipe diameter of each other
No two clamps within 0.5 m of each other
No two clamps within three pipe diameters of each other
No minimum spacing applies between clamps
source: Cl. 5.2: no two such clamps shall be installed within one pipe diameter of each other.

q: When a pipeline leak occurs at a KOC facility, to whom must it be reported in the first instance under KOC.SA.017?
options: Asset PSM Team within 10 working days
Contracts Group through the Clamp Register
source: Cl. 5.1: whenever a leak occurs it shall be reported to ERCU at 160 and all concerned per KOC.GE.007.

q: A pipeline leak is caused by general corrosion and shows signs of multiple leaks. Which repair means should be considered first?
options: A sealing band clamp at each leak point
Epoxy wrap over the corroded area
A bolt-on clamp on the largest leak only
source: Cl. 5.2: clamps are for localized pitting leaks; for general corrosion with multiple leaks, a split sleeve clamp should be considered first.

q: What minimum horizontal radius of warning barricade does KOC.SA.019 require around a hot-tapping site?
source: Cl. 5.3.1 xxii: hot-tapping site shall have a warning barricade with a horizontal radius not less than 15 m; mobile equipment kept upwind outside it.

q: When a line packer or seal plug is used, how must the end of its vent pipe be arranged?
options: At least 15 m away and left open to atmosphere
At least 30 m away and dipped in a water bucket
At least 30 m away and connected to the flare
At least 50 m away and fitted with an end cap
source: Cl. 4.4 / 5.3.3: vent pipe end kept at least 30 m away, dipped in a bucket of clear water, monitored continuously; stop work if bubbles appear.

q: Under KOC.SA.019, for which activity is the signature of the KOC Inspection Engineer required on the work permit?
options: All hot-tapping, welding and plugging work
source: Cl. 4.2: Inspection Engineer approval is required only for in-service welding, after confirming remaining wall thickness.

q: How should the hot-tapping machine be installed with respect to the operator's position?
options: So the operator stands downwind of the machine
So the operator stands upwind of the machine
So the operator stands directly above the cutter
Wind direction is not a consideration
source: Cl. 4.4: ensure the hot-tapping machine is installed in such a way that the operator is positioned in the upwind direction.

q: How must the weight of the hot-tapping machine be managed during the operation?
options: Rest fully on the pipeline being tapped
Be independently supported off the pipeline
Be held by a crane throughout the operation
Be supported on scaffolding tied to the pipe
source: Cl. 5.3.1 xix: the hot-tapping machine shall be independently supported; its weight shall not be transferred to the equipment being tapped.

q: Which statement about sparking tools is correct under KOC.SA.019?
options: They are prohibited during both hot-tapping and welding
They are allowed during hot-tapping but not during welding
They are not allowed during hot-tapping but are allowed during welding
They are allowed during both if a fire watch is present
source: Cl. 5.3.1 xviii: sparking tools shall not be used during hot tapping; however, they are allowed during welding.

q: During a plugging operation, which step is designated a 'HOLD POINT' to be witnessed by the Company's representative?
source: Cl. 5.3.3: installation of the gas plug shall be a 'HOLD POINT' witnessed by the Company's representative.

q: During hot-tapping, a leak develops at the machine flange. What must the Worksite Supervisor ensure first?
options: Retrieve the cutter, close the valve and stop safely
Continue cutting at reduced speed to finish the bore
Tighten the flange bolts while the machine is running
Have the fire watch spray the flange and continue
source: Cl. 4.4: if any hazardous situation (e.g. leak) is observed, ensure the cutter is retrieved, the isolation valve closed and hot work stopped safely.

q: While welding is in progress, within what radius of the work must the assigned Fire Watch remain until relieved?
source: Cl. 4.5: the Fire Watch shall remain within 8 m radius of the work vicinity during welding / cutting until relieved.

q: After a welding job is completed, how long must the Fire Watch remain at the location?
source: Cl. 4.5: remain at least 30 minutes after hot work until the area is inspected and found free of ignition sources.

q: Before welding in a plant area, flammable materials must be cleared, and drains covered with wet tarpaulins, within what distance of the worksite?
source: Cl. 5.7: flammable materials cleared at least 20 m away; all drains within 20 m covered with wet tarpaulins weighted with sandbags.

q: Under KOC.SA.021, acetylene must not be generated, piped or used at a pressure exceeding:
source: Cl. 5.4: under no condition shall acetylene be used at a pressure in excess of 15 psig (103 kPa gauge).

q: Why must fittings containing more than 70% copper (other than a burner tip) not be used in acetylene welding equipment?
options: Copper corrodes rapidly in contact with oxygen
Copper and acetylene form explosive copper acetylide
Copper conducts heat back and causes flashback
Copper lowers the flame temperature too much
source: Cl. 5.2: copper in contact with acetylene is liable to form a dangerous explosive compound, copper acetylide.

q: Which filter lens shade range does KOC.SA.021 specify for electric arc welding?
source: Cl. 5.3 Lens Shade Guide: arc welding 10–14; torch brazing 3–4; gas welding 4–8; cutting 3–6.

q: What minimum distance must an electric arc welding generator be kept from the hot work area?
source: Cl. 5.5: the welding generator should be kept at least 5 m away from the hot work area.

q: A pipe must be cold cut inside a hazardous area. Which equipment is permitted under KOC.SA.021?
options: Pneumatic cold cutting machine or manual cutter
Abrasive disc cutter with a spark guard
Any cutter, provided a fire watch is present
source: Cl. 5.6: in a hazardous area only pneumatic cold cutting machines and manual cutters are allowed; electric-driven cutting machines are not allowed.

q: Under the KOC multi-lock sequence for electrical isolation, who applies the FIRST lock?
options: The Permit Issuer, before issuing the permit
The Authorized Electrical Person, after confirming isolation
The Worksite Supervisor, after receiving the permit
The Shift Controller, after approving the request
source: Cl. 5.6 (i): the first lock shall be applied by the Authorized Electrical Person immediately after confirming electrical isolation.

q: On completion of work, what is the correct order for removing locks from the multi-lock device before electrical de-isolation?
options: Electrical Person, then Permit Issuer, then Worksite Supervisor
Permit Issuer, then Worksite Supervisor, then Electrical Person
Worksite Supervisor, then Permit Issuer, then Electrical Person
Shift Controller removes all locks together at one time
source: Cl. 5.6: the sequence is reversed for removal — Worksite Supervisor / Permit Applicant first, Permit Issuer second, Authorized Electrical Person last.

q: Which of the following is NOT considered an energy isolating device under KOC.SA.022?
options: A cut-out fuse on the supply circuit
source: Cl. 2.0: push buttons, selector switches and other control circuit type devices are not energy isolating devices.

q: Why does KOC.SA.022 state that Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs) should not be used as the point of disconnection?
options: They trip too easily under normal load
Positive contact separation cannot be confirmed
They cannot be fitted with any warning tag
They are only rated for very low voltages
source: Cl. 5.1 f): do not use MCBs as disconnections because confirming positive contact separation is generally not possible.

q: For multi-disciplinary jobs, KOC.SA.022 recommends colour-coded padlocks. Which colour is assigned to Operations?
source: Cl. 5.6: Yellow – Electrical / Blue – Operation / Black – Mechanical / Red – Instrument.

q: What is the minimum number of individually marked key storage boxes each facility must have for multi-lockout keys?
source: Cl. 5.7: each facility shall have at least 4 key storage boxes (Electrical, Mechanical, Instrumentation & Operation).

q: An urgent electrical isolation is needed to protect the plant and workforce. Under KOC.SA.022, how may it be authorized?
options: Verbally by the Authorized Electrical Person or Shift Controller
Only after a written Electrical Isolation Certificate is approved
Verbally by any Worksite Supervisor who is present at site
Only by the Asset HSE Team after carrying out a site visit
source: Cl. 5.4: emergency isolation can be carried out immediately by verbal approval of the Authorized Electrical Person or Shift Controller; written formalities completed once the emergency is over.

q: After isolating and locking an electrical motor, how must the absence of voltage be confirmed before work starts?
options: By pressing the local start button to check it does not run
By testing with an appropriate and tested voltage tester
By checking the breaker indicator light is off
By confirming with the Control Room Operator by radio
source: Cl. 4.4 / 5.1 j)–k): verify isolation by electrical measurement; presence of voltage must be tested using an appropriate and tested voltage tester.

q: According to the KOC.SA.024 JSA flow, who initiates, reviews and authorizes a JSA, respectively?
options: Permit Applicant, Permit Issuer, HSE Team
Worksite Supervisor, Permit Applicant, Permit Issuer
Safety Officer, Worksite Supervisor, Permit Applicant
Permit Issuer, Permit Applicant, Worksite Supervisor
source: Cl. 5.9 / Appendix 1: JSA initiated by Worksite Supervisor, reviewed by Permit Applicant, authorized by Permit Issuer.

q: For which activities does KOC.SA.024 require a JSA WITH Task Risk Assessment (initial and residual risk)?
source: Cl. 2.0 / 5.4: JSA with Task Risk Assessment will be carried out only for critical activities.

q: A contractor submits a JSA copied from a similar job at another gathering centre. Under the 2025 revision of KOC.SA.024, this is:
options: Acceptable if the Permit Issuer signs it
Prohibited; a task-specific JSA is needed
Acceptable if reviewed at the toolbox talk
source: Cl. 5.1 Note: the use of generic JSA is strictly prohibited; a standalone JSA specific to the exact task, location and worksite conditions must be developed.

q: In KOC.SA.024, 'residual risk' is best defined as the risk:
options: Present before any controls are applied
Remaining after controls have been applied
Linked to the worst credible outcome only
Accepted by the Permit Issuer without controls
source: Cl. 2.0: residual risk is the risk remaining after controls have been applied to associated hazards that have been identified.

q: What size of Risk Assessment Matrix (Severity vs Likelihood) is used in the current KOC JSA template?
source: Revision 3 Aug 2025 / Appendix 1: RAM changed to 6x6 Severity vs Likelihood to align with KOC.GE.018.

q: When a JSA is prepared for a job that involves the use of chemicals, what should it include?
options: A review of the Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
A medical surveillance record for each worker
source: Cl. 5.5: JSAs for jobs that involve the use of chemicals should include a review of SDS sheets.

q: On completion of a job carried out under a work permit, where is the JSA sheet retained as a record?
options: With the Permit Issuer, in file
It is discarded once the permit is closed
source: Cl. 5.7: on completion, the JSA sheet shall be retained in file with the Permit Issuer (routine work without permit: with the Controlling Team).

q: A Task Risk Assessment shows the residual risk remains in the intolerable region and engineering alternatives are not feasible. Under the KOC JSA risk regime, the activity may proceed only:
options: With Manager-level endorsement and a risk-reduction action plan
If the Worksite Supervisor holds an extra toolbox talk on it
If the Permit Issuer marks the permit as a critical activity
If additional PPE is issued to every worker on the task
source: Appendix 1 Risk Control Regime: intolerable risk — activity shall only proceed upon KOC Management endorsement (Manager and above) supported by a detailed action plan.

q: During excavation in an EOD-certified area, a worker uncovers a suspected unexploded shell. What is the correct sequence of first actions?
options: Lift it out carefully and carry it away from the trench
Leave it untouched, clear and mark the area, move away, call 160
Photograph it close up on a mobile phone and send it to HSE
Cover it with sand and carry on in another part of the trench
source: Cl. 5.2.4: do not touch; stop work and clear area; mark location at a safe distance; move away before using radio/phone; inform Fire Station / 160; request EOD assistance.

q: Before electric shot firing with electric detonators, all radio communication equipment within what range must be switched off?
source: Cl. 5.1.3.3: handheld radios / transmitters not within 150 m; all radio equipment within 150 m switched off before electric shot firing.

q: A charge fired by safety fuse has misfired. What is the minimum time before anyone may approach it?
source: Cl. 5.1.3.2: no one should approach until not less than 30 minutes (safety fuse) or 10 minutes (electric firing) has elapsed.

q: Under KOC.SA.025, no naked flame, spark or source of ignition is permitted within what distance of an explosive storage facility?
source: Cl. 5.1.1.2: any naked flame, spark or source of ignition shall not be permitted within 25 m (80 ft) of the explosive storage facility.

q: As a minimum, how far must a permanent explosive storage facility be located from any other building or place visited by employees or the public?
source: Cl. 5.1.1.1: permanent explosive storage must be at least 100 m from any other building, habitation or place liable to be visited.

q: Which arrangement for transporting explosives and detonators to a well site complies with KOC.SA.025?
options: Both in the same vehicle, in separate compartments
Both in the same container, if detonators are shunted
In separate vehicles, with no explosives in the driver's cab
Detonators in the driver's cab, explosives in the cargo bed
source: Cl. 5.1.2: explosives and detonators must be transported separately and not in the same vehicle; no explosive in the driver's cab.

q: What is the maximum number of charges that should be prepared and loaded for any single firing operation?
source: Cl. 5.1.3.1: a maximum of ten charges should be prepared and loaded for any single firing operation; count the shots fired.

q: A Controlling Team wants to start work in a new desert area. Which form of EOD clearance is acceptable under KOC.SA.025?
options: Verbal confirmation from the EOD contractor's supervisor
A printed EOD certificate with the cleared area marked on a map
An e-mail from any HSE Officer stating the area is clear
A note on the Permit to Work that the area appears clear
source: Cl. 5.2.3: EOD certification shall be issued on printed format with extent of clearance marked on a map; verbal clearance is not acceptable.

q: What is the minimum distance from a hydrocarbon-carrying pipeline within which mechanical excavation (including levelling with an excavator) is prohibited?
source: Cl. 5.4 b): no mechanical excavation closer than 5 m to any hydrocarbon carrying pipeline, even for levelling.

q: Without a Management of Change and risk assessment, mechanical excavation should not take place closer than what distance to non-hydrocarbon pipelines, cables and services?
source: Cl. 5.4 c): no mechanical excavation closer than 3 m to non-hydrocarbon pipelines, cables and services; MOC and risk assessment if closer.

q: In a trench deeper than 1 m, how must access ladders be provided under KOC.SA.026?
options: Projecting 0.5 m above the edge, every 15 m of travel
Projecting 1 m above the edge, every 7.5 m of lateral travel
Projecting 1 m above the edge, every 15 m of lateral travel
Projecting 1.5 m above the edge, at each end only
source: Cl. 5.4 i): ladder projecting minimum 1 m above the edge; ladders every 7.5 m (25 ft) of lateral travel, secured top and bottom.

q: For an excavation up to 1.2 m deep, what is the minimum distance excavated material (spoil) must be placed from the edge?
source: Cl. 5.4 l): excavated material shall be placed not less than 1 m from the edge for depth up to 1.2 m, increased in proportion to depth.

q: Heavy equipment, materials and excavating machinery must be kept at least how far from the excavation area?
source: Cl. 5.4 n): heavy equipment, material or excavating machinery shall be kept clear from the excavation area by at least 3 m.

q: Which barricading arrangement around an open trench meets KOC.SA.026?
options: Barrier tape tied between steel rebars
Hard fixed barriers with reflective warning signs
Rope strung between rebars at each corner
Spoil heaped along the edge as a bund
source: Cl. 4.3 / 5.4 k): hard fixed barriers with reflective warning notices, signs and flashing lights; tapes and rebars shall not be used as barriers.

q: An excavation in Type B soil will exceed 1 m in depth. Which shoring arrangement meets KOC.SA.026?
options: No shoring if the sides are sloped at 30°
Sheeting 450 mm above ground; boards ≤ 750 mm apart
Polling boards 2 m apart; braces 2 m apart
No shoring if the trench is under 2 m deep
source: Cl. 5.6.1.2 a): Type B over 1 m — shoring required; sheeting at least 450 mm above ground; polling boards ≤ 750 mm apart; horizontal braces ≤ 1 m apart.

q: In addition to the Excavation Notification, which work permit is required for excavation using a mechanical excavator?
source: Cl. 5.3 e) / 5.6.2: a Hot Work Permit is required for excavation involving a mechanical excavator; a Cold Work Permit for manual excavation.

q: How does KOC.SA.027 define 'High Voltage'?
options: A system voltage of 1000 V and above
A system voltage of 3300 V and above
source: Cl. 2.0: High Voltage – a system voltage of 3300 volts and above; Low Voltage – not exceeding 440 volts.

q: Portable tools and extension cords above 50 V to ground that are frequently plugged and unplugged must be protected by an RCD with a maximum trip setting of:
source: Cl. 5.1: such equipment must be protected by permanent or portable RCDs with a 30 mA maximum current setting.

q: A crane must pass under an existing 132 kV overhead power line. What is the minimum vertical clearance required between the lowest conductor and the top of the equipment?
source: Cl. 5.1 table: for 33 kV & 132 kV lines, minimum vertical safety clearance from lowest conductor to top of equipment is 5 m (10 m from ground).

q: A portable hand lamp on a trailing lead is needed inside a confined space. What does KOC.SA.027 require?
options: Supply not exceeding 24 V and explosion-proof type
Supply not exceeding 110 V with an RCD
Supply not exceeding 240 V with double insulation
Any lamp, if the space is gas free
source: Cl. 5.2: for a portable hand lamp on a trailing lead inside a confined space, supply voltage shall not exceed 24 V and only explosion-proof type shall be used.

q: When an isolated LV/HV conductor is earthed by installing a copper earthing conductor, what is its minimum cross-section?
source: Cl. 5.3 C: each conductor shall be earthed by fixed earthing switch, CB, or a copper conductor of minimum cross section 25 sq. mm.

q: Before starting work inside a substation protected by a CO2 or clean-agent suppression system, what must the authorized electrical person do?
options: Disable the fire alarm panel for the whole shift
Switch the system to Manual/Maintenance mode
Open all doors so any released gas can escape
Keep the system on Auto and wear an SCBA set
source: Cl. 4.4 / 5.3 A: turn the system to Manual/Maintenance mode on entry and return it to Normal (Auto) mode after the job and evacuation; record in the logbook.

q: A worker is unconscious and still in contact with an electrical source. What does KOC.SA.027 say should be done first?
options: Pull the victim away by the clothing
Free the victim using a Rescue Stick
Pour water on the equipment to trip it
source: Cl. 5.2: the victim should be removed safely from the electrical source by means of a Rescue Stick and artificial respiration given by trained personnel.

q: Under the 'Test Before Touch' requirement of KOC.SA.027, how must the voltage tester itself be checked?
options: Only once a year when it is calibrated
On a known live source before and after use
Only before use, with its self-test button
Not needed when the tester is brand new
source: Cl. 5.1: Test Before Touch includes verifying test instruments on a known energized source before and after the test for absence of voltage.

q: Before cutting an isolated high voltage cable, what must be done at the point of cut?
options: Wrap the cable with insulating tape
Spike it with a spiking gun or earthed spike
Test insulation resistance at 5 kV first
Hang a caution notice at the cut point
source: Cl. 5.3 D: HV cables shall be spiked at the point where they are to be cut by a spiking gun or a wooden-shafted, earthed steel-shod spike.

q: A single crane will lift a load equal to 80% of its rated capacity at the planned radius. Under KOC.SA.029, this lift is:
options: A standard lift, since it is below 100% of capacity
A critical lift, because it exceeds 75% of rated capacity
A critical lift only if it also exceeds 50 tonnes
A standard lift if it is done in daylight
source: Cl. 2.0 Critical lift: loads exceeding 75% of the rated capacity of any one crane.

q: Which of the following lifts is classified as a critical lift by height under KOC.SA.029?
options: A lift exceeding 10 m in height
A lift exceeding 20 m in height
A lift exceeding 30 m in height
A lift exceeding 50 m in height
source: Cl. 2.0 Critical lift: lifts which exceed 30 m in height (also > 50 tonnes, > 75% capacity, multiple cranes, man-lifting, etc.).

q: What is the minimum age for an operator of load handling equipment under KOC.SA.029?
source: Cl. 2.0 Operator: should be minimum 21 years of age, with 3rd party training certificates for the equipment.

q: A lifting sling is inspected in November. According to the KOC.SA.029 quarterly colour code, which colour should it carry?
source: Cl. 5.2: Q1 Apr–Jun Green; Q2 Jul–Sep Yellow; Q3 Oct–Dec Blue; Q4 Jan–Mar White.

q: Above what wind speed at the personnel platform must a man-lifting operation not begin, or be terminated if in progress?
source: Cl. 5.6.5: when wind speed exceeds 15 mph (24 km/h) at the personnel platform, man-lifting must not begin or must be terminated.

q: What minimum size of outrigger pad does KOC.SA.029 recommend under each crane outrigger float?
options: Same size as the outrigger foot
At least twice the size of the outrigger foot
At least three times the size of the outrigger foot
At least five times the size of the outrigger foot
source: Cl. 5.6.3: outrigger pad size should be at least three times the size of the outrigger foot.

q: When must a wire rope be removed from service due to broken wires under KOC.SA.029?
options: When any single broken wire is found
When broken wires exceed 10% in 8 diameters
When broken wires exceed 25% in one lay
Only when a full strand is broken
source: Cl. 5.8.3: wire rope shall not be used if, in any length of eight diameters, total visible broken wires exceed 10% of total wires.

q: What is the maximum speed at which material handling equipment (e.g. a forklift) may be driven while operating inside a company facility?
source: Cl. 5.8.4: the equipment shall not be driven at a speed exceeding 8 km per hour while operating in a company facility.

q: A contractor installs a fixed tower crane at a KOC site. What is the maximum validity of the Controlling Team's approval before the approval process must be repeated?
source: Cl. 5.3: approval for contractor fixed / permanently installed load handling equipment shall not exceed 12 months.

q: Unless conditions warrant greater clearance, painting should not be carried out within what distance of potential ignition sources such as welding or flame cutting?
source: Cl. 5.10: no painting should be carried out within 75 feet of potential ignition sources.

q: Which surface preparation method is prohibited under KOC.SA.030?
source: Cl. 5.4: sand blasting is prohibited.

q: Which of the following must NOT be used for solvent cleaning of surfaces before painting?
options: Alkali cleaners from an approved supplier
source: Cl. 5.4: benzene, gasoline, carbon tetrachloride and chlorinated hydrocarbons with low TLVs (< 20 ppm) shall not be used for solvent cleaning.

q: If practical alternatives exist, solvents and paints shall not be applied to surfaces warmer than:
source: Cl. 5.10: solvents and paints shall not be applied to surfaces warmer than 80°C if practical alternatives exist (and not flushed into containers hotter than 50°C).

q: A painter suffers a small skin puncture from high-pressure fluid from an airless spray gun. What does KOC.SA.030 require?
options: Clean with solvent and apply a plaster
Continue work and report at the end of shift
Wash with soap and monitor for 24 hours
source: Cl. 5.5: emergency medical care shall be obtained immediately if any high pressure fluid penetrates the skin; injection injuries can be extremely serious.

q: Inside a confined space, during which activities must all personnel wear respirable air-fed hoods under KOC.SA.030?
options: Only during abrasive blasting of surfaces
Only during airless spray painting work
During blasting, spraying, solvent or brush work
Only when the LEL reading exceeds 10%
source: Cl. 5.8: air-fed hoods shall be worn inside confined spaces whenever blasting or spray painting, solvent cleaning or brush painting is in progress.

q: Where should paint or thinner be decanted from one container to another?
options: Inside the store, near the shelves
In the open air, away from hazardous operations
Inside the spray booth, exhaust running
At the work face, beside the item painted
source: Cl. 5.11: dispensing or decanting shall not take place within the store but in the open air away from areas of hazardous operations.

q: What must be done whenever an airless spray gun is left unattended?
options: Point the gun into the paint bucket
source: Cl. 5.5: the trigger safety catch shall be engaged whenever the airless gun is left unattended; tip guard always in place while spraying.

q: Under KOC.SA.031, an activity is defined as 'work at height' when it is carried out at an elevated location higher than:
source: Cl. 2.0: work at height is an activity at an elevated location of more than 1.8 m (6 ft) from the working ground level.

q: What minimum load must a fixed anchor point be capable of supporting for each person attached to it?
source: Cl. 2.0 / 5.2.3.3: an anchorage must be capable of supporting at least 5,000 lb (22.2 kN) for each person attached.

q: Which lanyard specification complies with KOC.SA.031 for use with a full body harness?
options: Max 1.8 m, shock absorber, self-locking hooks
Max 3 m, made of polypropylene rope
Any length, shortened by tying knots
source: Cl. 5.2.3.2: maximum lanyard length 1.8 m (6 ft), self-locking hooks each end, shock absorber; never shortened with knots; no polypropylene.

q: As a general guideline, at what length of climb on a fixed ladder must appropriate fall protection be provided?
source: Cl. 5.2.2: appropriate fall protection must be provided whenever the length of climb on a fixed ladder equals or exceeds 24 ft (7.3 m).

q: Which guardrail arrangement meets the KOC.SA.031 edge protection requirements?
options: Top rail 750 mm high; no mid rail needed
Top rail ≥ 950 mm; no gap over 470 mm
Top rail 1,200 mm; gaps up to 600 mm
Steel banding as top rail at 1,000 mm
source: Cl. 5.2.1 / 5.2.3.8: main guard rail at least 950 mm (normally 1,000 mm); no gap more than 470 mm; steel/plastic banding not permitted as rails.

q: Which statement about personal fall arrest equipment is correct under KOC.SA.031?
options: A body belt may be used if it has a shock absorber
Body belts are prohibited; harness with 100% tie-off
100% tie-off is needed only above 6 m in height
One lanyard is enough when moving between anchors
source: Cl. 5.2.3.1: full body harness with two shock-absorbing lanyards; use of a body belt for fall arrest is prohibited; ensure 100% tie-off.

q: In addition to the user's visual pre-use check, how often must the Controlling Team ensure harnesses, lanyards and lifelines are formally inspected and tagged?
source: Cl. 5.3: all fall-arresting equipment shall be subjected to a monthly inspection program and tagged if fit for use.

q: A worker's lanyard arrested a short fall, and the shock absorber appears undamaged. What does KOC.SA.031 require?
options: Re-use it after a careful visual check
Re-use it after re-packing the absorber
Use it for work restraint only
source: Cl. 5.2.3.2 / 5.3: components subjected to impact loading shall be removed from service; equipment involved in a fall must not be used again.

q: Use of a crane-suspended man basket to lift workers is permitted only in exceptional cases. How must the lift be classified and planned?
options: As a standard lift with a JSA only
As a critical lift with a Critical Lift Plan
As routine work not requiring a permit
As a standard lift if fitted with guardrails
source: Cl. 5.2.2: use of a man basket shall be considered a critical lift; a Critical Lift Plan shall be prepared per KOC.SA.029.

q: In a cylinder store, oxygen cylinders must be separated from fuel-gas cylinders by a minimum of:
options: 3 m, or a 1 m high barrier
6.1 m, or a 1.5 m high fire-rated barrier
10 m, with no barrier option allowed
15 m, or any solid wall of any height
source: Cl. 5.4: oxygen separated from fuel-gas cylinders by at least 20 ft (6.1 m) or a non-combustible barrier at least 5 ft (1.5 m) high, ½-hour fire resistance.

q: According to the hose colour coding in KOC.SA.035 (BS EN ISO 3821), which colour hose is used for acetylene?
source: Cl. 5.7: Blue – Oxygen; Red – Acetylene; Orange – Propane, LPG, Natural Gas or Fuel Gas.

q: Compressed gas cylinders must not be exposed to temperatures (including direct sunlight) exceeding:
source: Cl. 5.4: any cylinder containing compressed gas shall not be subjected to a temperature exceeding 54.5°C (130°F).

q: Why must acetylene cylinders be stored, handled and used in the vertical position?
options: To let the porous mass settle evenly
To stop liquid acetone escaping to the valve
To keep the cylinder cooler in sunlight
To make the colour code easier to read
source: Cl. 5.1: acetylene is dissolved in acetone; cylinders must be kept vertical to prevent liquid acetone escaping and damaging valves and equipment.

q: As a means of distinguishing gases, which valve outlet thread is used on acetylene, hydrogen and other flammable gas cylinders?
source: Cl. 5.2: right-hand thread for oxygen and non-flammable gases; left-hand thread for acetylene, hydrogen and flammable gases.

q: A flashback occurs during oxy-acetylene cutting, but the hose looks intact from outside. What must be done with the hose?
options: Purge it with oxygen and continue the job
Leak test with soapy water and re-use if OK
Discard it immediately; the inner wall is damaged
Cut off the last metre and re-use the rest
source: Cl. 5.7: any hose in which a flashback has occurred will have its inner wall damaged and must be discarded immediately.

q: After opening a gas cylinder valve fully for use, how should it be left?
options: Fully open against the back stop
A half turn back from full open
Fully open and taped in position
source: Cl. 5.5: an open valve shall be left a half turn back from full open so that movement to the back stop indicates the valve is open.

q: 'Snifting' (briefly opening a cylinder valve to clear dirt before fitting a regulator) is permitted for most gases. For which gas is it NEVER allowed?
source: Cl. 5.5: hydrogen shall never be snifted as it may ignite spontaneously.

q: According to KOC.HE.003, what is the permissible flammable gas limit for authorized cold work?
source: Cl. 5.6.1: the permissible limit for authorized cold work is below 10% of the LEL (hot work: 0% LEL).

q: Where periodic gas testing is used during hot or cold work, the test interval must not exceed:
source: Cl. 5.6.1 / 5.6.3: testing continuously or periodically with the test interval not exceeding two hours.

q: When gas testing for hot work, the gas test area shall include everywhere within what distance of the hot work location?
source: Cl. 5.7: the gas test area shall include everywhere within 50 ft (15 m) of the hot work location.

q: A confined space is being mechanically ventilated by an exhaust fan. When should the gas test be carried out?
options: While the fan is running at full speed
Immediately after switching the fan off
About 10 minutes after stopping the exhaust fan
Only after the fan has been removed from the manway
source: Cl. 5.7: for a mechanically ventilated confined space, test only after 10 minutes of stopping the exhaust fan to avoid the effect of air draft.

q: Which acceptable exposure levels (TLV-TWA) does KOC.HE.003 state for carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide?
source: Cl. 5.3: acceptable levels — carbon monoxide 25 ppm (TLV-TWA, ACGIH) and sulphur dioxide 5 ppm (TLV-TWA, KEPA).

q: Under the TLV-STEL definition in KOC.HE.003, exposures above the TLV-TWA up to the STEL should be:
options: Less than 15 minutes each, no more than 4 times a day, at least 60 minutes apart
Less than 30 minutes each, no more than 2 times a day, at least 30 minutes apart
Less than 15 minutes each, unlimited times a day
Less than 60 minutes each, once a day
source: Cl. 2.0: exposures above TWA up to STEL should be < 15 minutes, no more than four times per day, with at least 60 minutes between them.

q: Which type of portable gas detector must be used for all INITIAL gas tests under KOC.HE.003?
options: Aspirated monitor with built-in sampling pump
Single-gas H2S badge clipped on the collar
Fixed area gas detector at the facility
source: Cl. 5.4.1: aspirated gas monitors (built-in pump) — all initial gas tests shall be done with this type of detector.

q: When testing a vessel where H2S could be present, where is it essential to sample?
options: As close to the top of the vessel as possible
Only at the manway opening of the vessel
As close to the bottom of the vessel as possible
Only through the vessel's vent line
source: Cl. 5.5 / 5.7: H2S is heavier than air (1.19); sample as close to the bottom as possible.

q: A gas detector is taken from an air-conditioned office to a hot outdoor worksite. What does KOC.HE.003 advise before using it?
options: Use it immediately, as sensors are temperature compensated
Allow 5–30 minutes for the instrument to stabilize to the temperature
Re-calibrate it in the field with test gas every time
Keep it in a plastic bag to avoid condensation during the test
source: Cl. 5.1: allow sufficient time for the equipment to temperature stabilize prior to use, which may vary between 5–30 minutes.

q: A contractor has 120 workers at a site. Under KOC.HE.004, what is the minimum number of first aiders required?
source: Cl. 5.4.1 c): one first aider per every 50 employees / contract workers (minimum one). 120 workers → 3 first aiders.

q: What is the required provision of first aid kits under KOC.HE.004?
options: One kit per facility, regardless of numbers
source: Cl. 5.5 / 5.8: one first aid kit shall be made available for every 50 workers.

q: To remain appropriately qualified, how often must a KOC first aider attend a first aid refresher course?
source: Cl. 5.5 B: first aiders attend refresher training courses every three (3) years.

q: How often must designated first aiders attend a CPR and AED training session?
source: Cl. 5.5 B / 5.6.1: attend CPR & AED training session once every year.

q: Under KOC.HE.004 and Kuwait labour requirements, a contractor must establish a First Aid Room wherever how many workers are engaged?
source: Cl. 5.4.1 a) / 5.5 II A: a First Aid Room shall be established wherever fifty (50) or more workers are engaged.

q: Which statement about first aid kit containers is correct under KOC.HE.004?
options: Locked, to prevent theft of contents
Clearly labelled, visible and not locked
Opened only by the site medic
source: Cl. 5.8.1: the first aid container should be prominently displayed, labelled 'First Aid Box', accessible, and should not be locked.

q: Within what time must a first aid case be reported in MyHSSE under KOC.HE.004 (with KOC.GE.007)?
source: Cl. 4: report in MyHSSE within 24 hours of incident occurrence (as per KOC.GE.007 & KOC.HE.020).

q: Which statement best describes the role of a first aider under KOC.HE.004?
options: Give initial care within training; refer to medical advice
Provide ongoing treatment until full recovery
Prescribe medicines from the first aid kit stock
Decide whether the injury needs to be reported
source: Cl. 5.6: first aiders undertake initial treatment consistent with training; when in doubt recommend medical advice; not responsible for ongoing care.

q: In an open yard storage area, what is the maximum height to which combustible materials may be piled?
source: Cl. 5.2.1: combustible materials shall in no case be piled higher than 20 ft (6.1 m).

q: What minimum width must driveways between and around combustible storage piles be kept?
source: Cl. 5.2.1: driveways between and around combustible storage piles must be at least 15 ft (4.57 m) wide.

q: Under KOC.GE.034, combustible material may NOT be stored outdoors within what distance of a building or structure?
source: Cl. 5.2.1: no combustible material may be stored outdoors within 10 ft (3.048 m) of a building or structure.

q: In an indoor store with sprinklers, what minimum clearance must be kept between the top of stored material and the sprinkler deflectors?
source: Cl. 5.2.2: clearance of at least 36 inches (0.9144 m) must be maintained between stored material and sprinkler deflectors.

q: Non-compatible materials that may create a fire, explosion or reaction hazard must be segregated in storage by a barrier with a fire resistance of at least:
source: Cl. 5.2.2: non-compatible materials must be segregated by a barrier having a fire resistance of at least 1 hour.

q: Where needed for access to doors, windows or standpipe connections, aisles must be kept at least how wide?
source: Cl. 5.3: keep aisles at least 3 ft (0.9144 m) wide where necessary for access to doors, windows or standpipe connections.

q: What does KOC.GE.034 recommend regarding end-of-day cleaning on construction sites?
options: Cleaning is done by a separate night crew only
Work stops half an hour early for site cleaning
Housekeeping is done once a week on rest day
Cleaning is needed only before HSE inspections
source: Cl. 5.0 Note: it is highly recommended that construction activities cease half an hour before and that time be used for area cleaning / housekeeping.

q: Under KOC.GE.034, what must Team Leaders ensure regarding gasoline within the battery limits of KOC projects, facilities and drilling sites?
options: Gasoline may be stored in approved jerry cans up to 20 litres
No gasoline storage or refuelling is allowed
Gasoline may be stored if kept 15 m from buildings
Gasoline refuelling is allowed only during daylight
source: Cl. 4.1: ensure that no gasoline storage or its refuelling is allowed in the KOC jurisdiction battery limit of any projects / facilities / drilling sites.

q: A worker's personal H2S monitor goes into alarm near a sour wellhead. What is the correct immediate response under KOC.GE.036?
options: Run downwind to the nearest vehicle and drive off
Don escape set, check windsock, walk crosswind
Stay in place and wait for Control Room instructions
Help colleagues nearer the release before leaving
source: Cl. 5.x Escape from H2S Release: put on escape-only respirator, observe windsock, walk (don't run) crosswind to Control Room / muster point; do not attempt to rescue others.

q: When purchasing personal H2S monitors, KOC.GE.036 recommends two alarm set points. What are they?
options: First alarm at or below 5 ppm; second at or below 10 ppm
First alarm at or below 10 ppm; second at or below 15 ppm
First alarm at or below 15 ppm; second at or below 50 ppm
First alarm at or below 20 ppm; second at or below 100 ppm
source: Cl. 5.3 c): units should alarm at or below 10 ppm (TWA/8 hrs) for the first alarm and at or below 15 ppm (STEL/15 min) for the second.

q: According to KOC.GE.036 Table 2, when H2S is between 10 and 15 ppm, work without respiratory protection is permitted for:
options: 15 min, up to 4 times per shift
30 min, up to 2 times per shift
source: Table 2: between 10 to 15 ppm, work is permitted for a 15-minute period without RPE, up to 4 times during an 8-hour shift.

q: Gas testing shows 60 ppm H2S at a worksite and the source cannot be isolated, purged or ventilated. Under KOC.GE.036, what is required for work to proceed?
options: No work is allowed above 50 ppm
source: Table 2: up to 100 ppm, work is permitted with positive-pressure supplied air respirator or 30-min SCBA only if the source cannot be isolated; above 100 ppm entry only for rescue.

q: Where should a personal H2S monitor be worn?
options: Inside the coverall pocket, away from dust
On the belt at waist level
source: Cl. 5.3 c): worn outside clothing close to the head, as this is where H2S will be ingested; shoulder or breast pocket is optimal.

q: A crew of 14 workers will carry out maintenance in an area where H2S hazards may be present, but the facility itself is not sour. What gas detection does KOC.GE.036 require?
options: One personal gas monitor for the crew
No detector, as the facility is not sour
One personal monitor per five workers
source: Cl. 4 Field Workers c): one personal monitor per crew below 10 workers; more than 10 workers — a tripod-mounted portable multi-gas detector; sour facility — every worker carries one.

q: KOC.GE.036 defines 'sour' hydrocarbons as oil or gas containing H2S above:
source: Cl. 2.0: sour hydrocarbons contain more than 0.001%, i.e. 10 ppm of hydrogen sulphide.

q: Why can opening a vessel that handled sour product be hazardous even after it has been drained?
options: Dry pyrophoric iron sulphide can self-ignite in air
H2S turns lighter than air once the vessel is open
Rust deposits stop portable gas detectors working
Sulphur dioxide is released when water is added
source: Cl. 5.2 f): pyrophoric scale (ferrous sulphide) reacts exothermically with oxygen and, when dry, auto-ignites at ambient temperature.

q: How often must personnel who may enter H2S hazardous areas receive H2S awareness training under KOC.GE.036?
source: Cl. 5.4 a): personnel who may be required to enter H2S hazardous areas shall receive annual H2S awareness.

q: What is the minimum isolation standard required for entry into a vessel or confined space under KOC.PS.016?
options: Single block valve, locked and tagged
Double block and bleed valve isolation
ESD valve closed with actuator enabled
source: Cl. 5.1 / 5.5.1: the minimum isolation standard for vessel or confined space entry is positive isolation; it is mandatory for such entry.

q: Which is the PREFERRED method of achieving positive isolation according to KOC.PS.016?
options: Closing two block valves with an open bleed
Spool removal with rated blank flanges on the live ends
Inserting a spade only when spool removal is easier
Closing a single gate valve and locking it
source: Cl. 5.5.1: spool removal is the preferred method of positive isolation; spade insertion where spool removal is not reasonably practicable; valves alone are not positive isolation.

q: Before breaking containment, how long does KOC.PS.016 recommend that isolation integrity tests be conducted, as a minimum?
source: Cl. 5.7: all isolations shall be tested and shown to be effective before containment is broken; integrity tests recommended for a minimum of 10 minutes.

q: What is the minimum recommended frequency for monitoring the integrity of isolation points while containment is broken?
options: Once per week, at the start of the work week
Once per day, at the start of day shift only
Once per shift and just before breaking containment
Only when the Work Party requests a check
source: Cl. 5.8: minimum recommended monitoring frequency is once per shift and immediately prior to breaking containment; results recorded at shift handover.

q: Which type of valve shall NOT be used as a form of isolation under KOC.PS.016?
options: Fail-closed ESD valve with actuator disabled
source: Cl. 5.9: non-return (check) valves, flow control valves and pressure relief valves shall not be used as a form of isolation.

q: During work under a double block and bleed isolation, the gauge on the bleed between the two block valves starts to show pressure. What must happen?
options: Open the bleed fully and continue working
Stop work and review and amend the isolation
Tighten the upstream valve and continue
Record it at shift handover and continue
source: Cl. 5.5.2: the void between block valves must remain at 0 barg; if pressure increases, work shall stop and the isolation be reviewed and amended.

q: Besides vessel entry, KOC.PS.016 recommends positive isolation for long-duration isolations. What duration is given as an example?
source: Cl. 5.5.1: positive isolation recommended for long duration isolations, e.g. more than one week, hot work, and new/out-of-service equipment interfaces.

q: Under KOC.PS.016, how are bleeds and vents that form part of an isolation to be controlled?
options: Padlocked shut like the block valves
Left untagged so they can be operated
Tagged and recorded, without a lock
Removed from the line and blanked
source: Cl. 5.13: bleeds and vents do not require a securing device, as their position may change, but they require a bleed/vent tag and must be documented on the Certificate.
